newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Countrywide to report strong 1st half profit.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Countrywide to report strong 1st half profit.

text.p: Countrywide Banking Corporation Managing Director David Wolfenden said on Friday the Bank of Scotland-owned group would report a strong rise in first half profit.
Countrywide is due to report for the six months to August 31 in a couple of weeks.
"It will show very strong growth for us again, which is consistent with the growth we've shown in the last couple of years," Wolfenden told Reuters in an interview.
"Our actual growth performance and our profit performance is significantly up on the comparable half-year."
Wolfenden said the growth was driven by volume, but margins in New Zealand continued to contract.

"On a half-year to half-year comparison, our margin squeeze continues. We've been able to maintain our fee income but our growth over the last two years is now paying revenue dividends on a volume basis and we've been able to to maintain our costs at a pretty static level on a year-on-year comparison," he said.
"Margins have again contracted for about the third year in a row in New Zealand, if not longer, actually."
Countrywide reported tax-paid profit of NZ$42 million in the year to February 29. Its net after tax profit for the six months to August 31, 1995 was NZ$21 million.
